messages.author: 680a113b1862eedc
messages.subject: significance threshold for interactions
parts:
Hi.
I'm an extreme novice at R/qtl (i.e. i started last week). I'm mostly
interested in finding epistasis between nonadditive QTLs (admittedly
in response to reviewer requests!). Luckily, I've gotten to the point
where I create the heat map and generate the (in my case) 4 page long
list of lod scores.

My question is... how do you determine the significance threshold for
a particular trait?

I thought I'd put the question out there before I screw everything up.
Thus far, I've run permutations with scantwo, but like it says in the
manual, that takes a LONG time (i have 28 traits...)! i've also added
the "hot" interactions to my formula for the fitqtl command. None of
my "hot spots" were significant when compared to the significance
threshold given by scantwo, but 3 were significant in the ANOVA table.
What have I done?!
Thank you very much!

[background: i'm working with a backcross mapping populations between
two plant species and ~80% of the markers were genotyped]

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] significance threshold for interactions
parts:
See our discussion of the interpretation of scantwo results at the
following:

http://www.rqtl.org/tutorials/new_summary_scantwo.pdf

I would start with 100 permutations for a single trait, to get a sense
of the numbers.

karl
